## 614b8ee6-6a63-4ee9-b948-d4fb9064d6be / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The experiment-11 continuation is the strongest current lineage: it achieved 776/800 successes across four disjoint development panels, while experiment 12 tied or slightly underperformed it on a further panel. Residual failures repeatedly occur near the negative angular edge and include both tolerance non-entry and brief entry followed by hold loss. These observations concern one coupled direct-torque behavior spanning the singular reset, posture choice, approach, settling, and sustained regulation.

**Lessons and limits:** The experiment-11 sampler improved complete success over its predecessor without establishing why, and the experiment-12 hold-credit consequence did not improve the shared edge failures. The latest reference and proxy-peak policies each had five negative-edge non-entry failures; the later experiment-12 checkpoint added one interrupted hold. Earlier representation, effort, boundary, action-mapping, and focused-exposure changes did not preserve broad competence under their tested conditions. Development evidence remains below the 98% objective, and failure stage or target geometry does not identify causal responsibility among branch choice, trajectory, braking, settling, and local regulation.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved how target radius and angle, the two inverse-kinematic branches, the reset singularity, direct-torque trajectory and velocity, settling, and sustained local regulation combine in the residual behavior. It is also unresolved whether the non-entry and interrupted-hold outcomes share a limitation, whether the observed angular asymmetry generalizes, and whether any improvement can preserve complete-task behavior across the full official distribution.
